data.name: Chaitri
data.gender_notes: Chaitri is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Chaitri is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Chaitra' meaning spring or the first month of the Hindu calendar. This name is associated with the arrival of new beginnings, joy, and radiance. The name Chaitri carries the meaning “Spring, Joyful, Radiant” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chaitri usually hope their child will grow to embody spring, joyful, radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the arrival of spring and new beginnings
data.etymology: Chaitri belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Spring, Joyful, Radiant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chaitri total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The Hindu month of Chaitra is considered auspicious for various reasons. One of the primary reasons is that it marks the beginning of the sacred Indian New Year. Many Indian festivals, including Holi, Ram Navami, and Hanuman Jayanti, fall in this month, signifying a period of celebration, happiness, and renewal.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Chaitri represents the awakening of new ideas, thoughts, and perspectives. It is a time for inner growth, self-reflection, and renewal of personal beliefs and values. During the month of Chaitra, many Hindus engage in fasting, meditation, and spiritual practices to cleanse their minds, bodies, and souls, thereby preparing for the upcoming spiritual festivals. The wishes and prayers made during this period are believed to be granted by the gods, opening the doors for personal progress and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Chaitri: Radiating with joy and creativity, embodying the vibrant energy of spring. Nurturing growth and happiness in all aspects of life.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Chaitri is mentioned in the Mahabharata as a month in the Hindu calendar The name Chaitri carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
